thread:
IncBot: INCIDENT — Serving cluster 'eu-west-1-serve' elevated to P1: sustained 5xx spike and node flaps detected. PagerDuty notified. :rotating_light:
Kira: paging @Jules (oncall). seeing lots of CUDA OOMs and IB timeouts across the RDMA-enabled pool.
Jules (oncall): on it. getting current blast radius now. which customer paths are failing?
Kira: summary: 11% 5xx rate on text-gen endpoints, tail latency up, and ~7 nodes in the rdma pool reported sudden NIC link transitions. stack shows cuda driver logs + rdma errors.
Sam: past hour we pushed a minor runtime change but only to dedicated-qa. logs show repeated: `cudaErrorUnknown: driver shutting down` and `/sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/events: port state change` interleaved.
Miguel: also seeing `rdma_cm: failed to resolve addr` and `ib_core` retransmit counters spiking. likely fabric-level packet loss.
Kira: mitigation plan attempt 1: scale down RDMA pool by 50% and shift traffic to non-RDMA nodes (cpu fallback) via routing rule. doing now.
Kira: routing change applied (canary -> 10% -> 100%). watch for error rate shift.
Jules (oncall): confirmed route change applied. error rate dropped to 6% within 90s, tail latency improving. still some OOMs in pods pinned to problematic nodes.
Sam: issuing cordon+drain on nodes: `kubectl cordon node-ix-34; kubectl drain node-ix-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for the top 3 offenders. restarting runtime containers with `--no-rdma` flag on restart as a short-term workaround.
Miguel: NetOps called — they see link flaps on ToR switch downstream of affected nodes. vendor ticket opened, they recommend disabling SR-IOV on NICs as a test and temporarily revert to kernel RDMA fallback.
NetOps Bot: Vendor ticket 231145 created. Estimated initial response in 45m.
Kira: customer impact assessment: ~18 tenants touched, 6 in prod with high severity; top-3 enterprise customers saw request latency >10s and intermittent truncation. Support notified and templated message drafted.
Jules (oncall): patching plan: 1) continue traffic shift, 2) drain bad nodes, 3) if vendor change needed, schedule rolling NIC firmware/driver update off-peak. anyone object?
Sam: doing drains now, one node failed to evict a container — container stuck in Terminating. log shows `SIGKILL` from kubelet then `OOMKilled` inside the runtime process. adding force delete.
Kira: grabbing a heap/profile from the crashed runtime to confirm memory accounting: attaching snippet:
```
[2024-06-12T14:02:03Z] runtime: meminfo: rss=22.8G cache=1.2G kv-cache=0.9G
[2024-06-12T14:02:05Z] runtime: cuda: allocation failed: out of memory, requested 2048MB
[2024-06-12T14:02:05Z] serving: fallthrough to fallback model (cpu) for request=tx-8a3f
```
Sam: looks like bursts of retransmits cause retransmit storms and GPU scheduling delays, pushing memory usage up and triggering OOM on some containers.
Miguel: NetOps suggests temporarily increasing NIC link-level timeouts to reduce spurious failovers and enabling ECN to reduce retransmit amplification. Only want to do that if vendor approves.
Jules (oncall): do we have a plan to prevent recurrence without hardware ops?
Kira: short-term: keep routing to non-RDMA nodes for at least 2 hours, set aggressive pod anti-affinity to avoid co-locating heavy-serving containers on the same host, and enable KV cache warming to reduce cold allocation spikes.
Sam: applied anti-affinity annotation to the serving deploy and bumped eviction threshold.
Miguel: NetOps will run continuous ibcounters and mlx_iov checks, sharing dashboard.
NetOps Bot: posting counters: `rx_drop=4200`, `tx_drop=3800`, `retransmits=19000` over last 10m.
Kira: customer comms: support sent initial notice to affected accounts with ETA and mitigation steps. no data loss reported; only availability degradation.
Jules (oncall): handing off to Miguel for next shift. summary in incident channel and PagerDuty set to low-noise until vendor reply. @Miguel you're POC for the postmortem.
Miguel: ack. I'll keep the routing rule in place until we have stable link metrics for 30m. will coordinate fw update window with vendor.
Kira: quick checklist for post-incident: - root cause: RDMA fabric packet loss causing retransmit storms -> GPU scheduling delays -> runtime OOM cascade. - mitigations: traffic failover, node drain, pod flag --no-rdma, vendor ticket, config changes (MTU/ECN/timeouts), anti-affinity + cache warm. - action owner list attached.
Sam: thrown in a temporary runtime healthcheck to detect early OOM growth and pre-emptively route sessions off node. will prod a PR for persistent healthprobe.
Miguel: opening postmortem draft and initial timeline. will include traffic graphs, ib counters, driver logs, node-level container restarts, and customer impact table.
Jules (oncall): thanks team — I'll stay nearby for any rapid re-escalation. great job stabilizing quickly. :raised_hands:
IncBot: INCIDENT update: status changed to "stabilized". elapsed duration ~53m. follow-up: postmortem owner Miguel.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged and closed in PD after follow-up schedule created.
Miguel: capturing action items: vendor FW update window, runtime patch to better handle rdma retransmit spikes, longer-term: graceful degrade to cpu models automatically on link anomalies. I'll post the postmortem link when ready.
Kira: adding a short runbook entry for oncall: steps to quickly fail traffic off RDMA pool and which flags to enable.
Jules (oncall): handoff complete. signing off.
